recipe: Goan coconut fish curry with lentil rice
servesNote: 2 portions — 905 kcal / 50 g protein each at £3.03/portion. ⭐ A coconut curry sharpened with vinegar — the Portuguese inheritance that makes a Goan curry taste Goan rather than generically creamy. The entire spice bill is zero.
adaptations: ⛔ THE RED LENTILS ARE OUT — finished 26 Aug and not replaced. Without the 50 g the 'lentil rice' is just rice, which works but loses the protein and the texture the side was there for. Cook 160 g of rice instead of 140 g and expect a slightly lighter plate.
⛔ THE COCONUT MILK IS NOT IN THE HOUSE either, and the creamed coconut that might have stood in for it is also out. This dish needs a shop.
⭐ THE HELD GINGER & GARLIC PASTE WOULD SAVE TWO MINUTES OF CHOPPING — except it is out too. Use the fresh garlic Tuesday bought and buy a thumb of ginger.
⭐ COD OR POLLOCK HOLD TOGETHER BETTER than basa and taste cleaner — add 2 minutes to step 9 if you use them.

prep: Cut the basa into large 4–5 cm chunks, bigger than feels necessary — ⛔ thin small pieces are the commonest cause of curry turning into fish soup. Pat every piece dry; basa carries a lot of water and wet fish thins your sauce.

Toss the fish with ½ tsp turmeric, a pinch of salt and the juice of half the lemon. Leave on a plate, 15 min minimum. ⭐ The salt firms the surface so pieces hold together, the turmeric seasons the flesh not just the sauce, and the acid takes the muddiness off farmed white fish.

steps.text: Rinse rice and lentils together until the water runs from milky to almost clear. Pan with 430 ml water, ½ tsp turmeric, bay, salt. Boil, stir ONCE, lid on, lowest heat, leave alone until the water is gone and small craters show on the surface. Off the heat, lid on, rest. Fluff before serving.
Heat the oil over medium. Add the cumin seeds and wait until they sizzle steadily and smell toasty (~30 sec) — ⚠️ if they darken fast the pan is too hot.
Add the onion and cook until completely floppy and translucent with brown at the edges, no crunch left at all. ⭐ Rushing this is why home curries taste raw and harsh.
Garlic, ginger, coriander stalks, split chilli. Fry until the raw garlic smell has gone and it smells sweet.

Ground cumin, remaining turmeric, paprika, cayenne. Stir into the oil until they darken a shade and smell nutty rather than dusty (30–45 sec), then immediately splash in water to stop them scorching. ⚠️ Burnt spice is bitter all the way to the plate.

Tomato and a pinch of salt, mashing with the spoon, until it has completely collapsed and you can see OIL GLISTENING AND SEPARATING at the edges of the masala. ⭐ That oil separation is the doneness cue in every Goan source consulted.

Coconut milk, ~150 ml water, the cider vinegar. Bring to a bare simmer — the surface should barely shiver. Never boil coconut milk hard. Season: it should taste slightly too salty and slightly too sharp, because the fish will dilute it.
Slide the fish in in a single layer, spoon sauce over each piece. ⛔ Now STOP STIRRING. To move the sauce, take the pan by the handle and rotate or shake it.

Cover and cook at that bare simmer until the fish has turned from grey-translucent to solid white and a piece nudged with a spoon FLAKES rather than bends. ⚠️ Basa is done sooner than it looks, and overcooking — not fish choice — is what makes this dish fall apart.
Off the heat: garam masala, coriander leaves, a little more lemon.
⭐ Stand 5 minutes with the lid on. Every Goan source says the curry improves as it sits.

Serve over the lentil rice with cold yoghurt on the side and a lemon wedge. ⛔ Don't stir the yoghurt in during cooking — it splits, and its job is cold sour contrast. Maria's next-day lunch: the sauce is better on day two, the fish is not. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water, covered, until just steaming — do not microwave on full power, which boils the sauce and turns basa to cotton wool.
